guidelines: Plan for 18-24 hours of actual coding time (account for sleep, meals, breaks)
Last 2-3 hours: Polish and presentation prep
Solo: Focus on one core feature, minimal scope
3-4 person: Can tackle more ambitious projects
Assign clear roles early: frontend, backend, design, presentation

sponsor-prizes: Best application in a domain (e.g., healthcare, education)

common-mistakes: Over-scoping: Trying to build too much
Late integration: Components don't work together
No demo: Can't show the product working
Poor presentation: Can't explain what you built
Ignoring sponsor requirements: Missing prize opportunities

planning: Identify the ONE core feature that demonstrates your idea
development: Mock external APIs if they're unreliable
Use feature branches for team projects
demo-preparation: Record a backup video demo in case of technical issues
Prepare a 2-minute pitch: problem, solution, demo, tech stack
Test the demo flow multiple times
Practice the pitch with your team
time-management: Hour 8-10: First integration test (get something working end-to-end)
Hour 18-22: Demo prep, slides, pitch practice

tips: Add screenshots and a demo video
Make the description skimmable (use headers, bullets)
Read API docs during planning phase
Check rate limits and free tier restrictions
Have a plan B if API is down or slow
For sponsor prizes, feature their API prominently

avoid-these: Building your own authentication system from scratch
Building mobile apps with native Swift/Kotlin (use React Native/Flutter)
Writing extensive tests (focus on working demo)
